name: consistency-violation-interface-init-on-external-type
description: An initial value on a data element typed by a stub. SWCraft does not know the stub's structure, so it cannot write a value specification that conforms to it; the element may still be typed by the stub, and it is the `init` that is refused.

context.summary: The `examples/basic` model with one implementation data type stub, `ForeignSpeed_T`. The change set creates an interface whose one data element is typed by the stub and carries an `init`.

authorization.notes: The scope covers the one address exactly, so the refusal is the model rule and not the authorization boundary.

input.intent: Publish the speed in the delivery's own type, starting at zero.

expected.notes: Two addresses: the `init` the repair removes, and the stub that makes it unanswerable, so a client can see both sides. The same finding is reported for a data element typed by a reference type whose chain of `base`s ends at a stub; it is decided before the `init` rules walk the type, so a stub-typed element never also reports an `init` shape finding for the same cause. Typing the element by the stub without an `init` is legal.
